title: You should run evals if you are seriously trading with your AI
author: Felixdaga1
selftext:
Hi folks, some of you might have seen my old posts here about the importance of evals if you are trading real money with AI. For example, how can u deploy it if you don't even know:

* Your AI returns if it was deployed a year ago
* IR impact from swapping to another model
* How a small change in prompt will affect its decisions

Running eval essentially means simulations on how your agent would behave and perform over a certain period, aka backtesting it. This is often more complicated and resource-intensive than setting up the agent because you have to enforce point-in-time controls; your agent can't pull prices/news beyond its decision date. You also need a bunch of supporting elements such as concurrency, standard output schema, runtime tracing...such that you can blast through iterations of your strategy or agent systematically and at speed to identify the optimal set up.

I have a fully automated [AI systematic strategy](https://www.fintel.capital/strategy) (developed while I was at BlackRock) deployed on >100k USD of my own capital so this is non-negotiable for me. I went through the pain of building a scalable platform for me to evaluate my own strategy, and now I'm open-sourcing it. Looking for people who are serious about trading with AI to try it out. Attached is a simple guide on how to leverage it

Note: You still need to know what you are doing - a strategy and agent in mind with access to whatever data you need. The platform just handles the grunts and make it scalable. It is handwork but once you do it a few times you won't go back to blindly deploying agents.
